# AnswerCue 2.8.2 — OpenAI response tiers

Choose your default OpenAI response tier in **Settings → AI Providers**, inside the OpenAI API key card. The choice saves automatically, takes effect on subsequent OpenAI requests, and persists across app restarts.

## Response tiers

- **Auto (project default):** follows your OpenAI project's configured service tier; preserves the previous app behavior.
- **Standard:** explicitly requests standard processing.
- **Fast (Priority):** requests faster processing for the selected OpenAI model, billed at the applicable premium rate.
- **Ultrafast:** explicitly uses GPT 6 Astra through the Responses API for OpenAI answers. The settings card explains the model override, higher pricing, and lower rate limits. It applies to text, screenshot analysis, and background OpenAI generation.

Test Connection now uses the saved response tier. Streaming, system prompts, image inputs, low reasoning, prompt cache keys, cancellation, and first-token timeouts are preserved. Ultrafast does not silently downgrade to another OpenAI model. Partial streams are not appended to by retries.

The existing Fast Response popup control remains a separate Groq feature. Response tiers do not change transcription, embeddings, custom providers, Gemini, Claude, or Codex CLI settings.

## Downloads and installation

- **Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4 and later):** `AnswerCue-2.8.2-arm64.dmg`.
- **Intel Macs:** `AnswerCue-2.8.2-x64.dmg`.
- macOS 12 or later. Drag AnswerCue into Applications from the DMG.
- This fork's initial macOS release is **ad-hoc signed, not Apple Developer ID signed or notarized**. Gatekeeper may block opening it. Use macOS Privacy & Security → Open Anyway if offered. Only install assets downloaded from this fork's release page.
- The release workflow verifies both architecture-specific DMGs and uploads DMGs, ZIPs, blockmaps, and updater metadata. Developer ID signing/notarization can be enabled with Apple repository secrets; manual builds can require signing explicitly.
- Update downloads and release notes now point to this fork.

## Validation and limitations

- Renderer production build and Electron build pass.
- Five new transport tests pass: explicit tier routing, Responses image/text conversion, streamed tokens, cancellation, and failure/incomplete handling.
- Settings selector checked in a browser with mocked Electron IPC for saving and reload persistence.
- The full suite retains the same 43 failures present in the unchanged fork (882 passed, 41 skipped after this change). Electron type checking also has pre-existing diagnostics; no new diagnostic categories were introduced.
- No paid OpenAI requests were made. Model/tier access, billing, real-world first-token latency, and manual macOS audio/permission smoke testing require validation on your account and Mac. Faster service tiers do not guarantee a fixed time to first token.
